newsitem.title: JAPAN: American freed by North Korea arrives in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: American freed by North Korea arrives in Tokyo.

text.p: A weary-looking Carl Hunziker, who had been detained in North Korea for three months, arrived in Tokyo on Wednesday with U.S. Congressman Bill Richardson, who negotiated the Korean-American's release.

Hunziker raised his hands in a victory salute the moment he stepped out of the door of the U.S. Air Force C-21 plane which flew him and Richardson from the North Korean capital of Pyongyang to the United States' Yokota air base on the outskirts of Tokyo.

"Congressman Richardson and Mr Hunziker have arrived in Japan," U.S. military spokesman Kevin Krejcarek told dozens of reporters and photographers at about 12.30 p.m. (0330 GMT) as they jostled for a sight of Hunziker at the air base amid light rain.
The 26-year-old Hunziker, who his family says is a missionary, was detained by North Korea near the Chinese border on August 24 and held on charges of espionage and illegal entry into North Korea.
The United States, South Korea and Hunziker's family have all denied he is a spy and say he accidentally strayed into North Korea while on a visit to China.

Richardson, a close confidant of President Bill Clinton, and Hunziker had been scheduled to leave North Korea for Tokyo on Tuesday. However, their departure was delayed for a day for reasons which were not yet known.
Richardson and Hunziker, both smiling widely, clasped hands and raised their arms above their heads as U.S. military personnel applauded the pair.
Hunziker, dressed in sweat pants and a military-style parka, walked unaided to a waiting car which whisked him off to the base's hospital for a medical examination.
